name: tpl-responded-existence-2-goal
task: If you move the ball, you must also take the key. Then pick up the box in the other room.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: the clauses match the task. Sentence 1 'If you move the ball, you must also take the key' is a condition with the no-timing cue 'also', so RespondedExistence(blocker_moved, has_door_key) hard is right, and blocker_moved correctly gets no Existence since it is only an if-condition. The 'Then' sentence makes picking up the box required after the key and, when it happens, after moving the ball: Existence(target_picked_up), Precedence(has_door_key, target_picked_up), and Response(blocker_moved, target_picked_up), all hard, are exactly the stated set, with correct argument order. The compiler's Redundant note on the RespondedExistence is not a defect: it is the 'if' rule the task's first sentence states, so it stays. The machine implements these clauses faithfully (u3 final only when the target is taken with the key already taken and any ball move followed, u1 rejecting when the box precedes the key or the key never follows a ball move).

texts: If the ball is moved, the matching door key must also be taken at some point.
The mission's target box must eventually be picked up.
The target box may be picked up only after the matching door key has been taken.
If the ball is moved, the target box must be picked up at or after that time.
